0235_identity_admission.schema.json.title: Identity admission and durable session capabilities
0235_identity_admission.schema.json.x-native-retention: Revoked JTIs remain authoritative through the supplied expiration-plus-refresh-grace time.
0235_identity_admission.schema.json.x-native-lock-order: User, then API key; JTI revocation uses one deterministic advisory transaction lock shared with the final-principal fence.

0236_identity_api_keys.schema.json.title: Identity API-key native command and receipt protocol
0236_identity_api_keys.schema.json.x-native-retention: Mutation receipts freeze only public key records and revoke outcomes, and cascade with their actor account.
0236_identity_api_keys.schema.json.x-native-lock-order: Lock the current actor and API-key credential through aap_identity_v1, then take the operation advisory lock, then lock a target key with FOR UPDATE NOWAIT.

0237_identity_sessions.schema.json.title: Identity native session command and receipt protocol
0237_identity_sessions.schema.json.x-native-retention: Success receipts freeze only issuance claims and cascade with their actor account.
0237_identity_sessions.schema.json.x-native-lock-order: Lock the current User row FOR UPDATE NOWAIT, then lock the presented JTI or API key through aap_identity_v1, then take the operation advisory lock before receipt replay or mutation.

0238_identity_accounts.schema.json.title: Identity native self-account commands and presence operator
0238_identity_accounts.schema.json.x-account-receipts: Only name, preference, password-change acknowledgements, and avatar-reference results are frozen; secrets and bearer tokens are never stored, and receipts cascade with their actor.
0238_identity_accounts.schema.json.x-account-lock-order: Acquire the current User lock before the JTI or API-key lock, then acquire a nonblocking operation lock and validate receipts. Preference writes wait for the User row; other account writes fail fast.

0239_identity_recovery.schema.json.title: Identity recovery, open registration and credential mail protocols
0239_identity_recovery.schema.json.x-token-migration: Existing challenge values are replaced in place by SHA-256 of their UTF-8 bytes; issued_email freezes the address used to issue each valid link.
0239_identity_recovery.schema.json.x-retention: Recovery operation receipts have no live User foreign key or raw name/email copy; registration replay reconstructs those two fields from the HMAC-matched request. Credential mail outbox secrets are encrypted with a separate mail key and cascade only with their actor account.
0239_identity_recovery.schema.json.x-lock-order: Serialize operation IDs first, then acquire User -> challenge -> outbox locks. No SQL lock is held during SMTP delivery.

0240_identity_groups.schema.json.title: Identity group catalog and assignment native capability
0240_identity_groups.schema.json.x-receipt: Receipts bind operation id, current actor id, operation, request fingerprint, derivation id and frozen data result; no raw bearer or audit metadata is stored.
0240_identity_groups.schema.json.x-lock-order: Try-lock operation id, inspect retained receipt, lock requested Group, key-share actor, no-key-update target Users, then Workspace Project and ProjectMember scope rows; replay never repeats Audit or rewinds state.

0241_identity_deactivation.schema.json.title: Identity self-deactivation and due-processing native capabilities

0241_identity_deactivation.schema.json.x-receipts: User receipts bind operation ID, actor ID, operation, request fingerprint, derivation ID, and frozen account result. Due receipts freeze every bounded page, including empty and blocked pages; neither receipt type has a User foreign key.
0241_identity_deactivation.schema.json.x-correlation-ledger: The request ledger stores request ID, User ID, requested/scheduled times, state, and native/legacy origin without a User foreign key or reason copy. Existing User lifecycle fields remain authoritative and pending requests survive administrative suspension/reactivation.
0241_identity_deactivation.schema.json.x-lock-order: Try the shared versioned super-admin invariant transaction lock before any User row lock. Self commands lock User FOR UPDATE NOWAIT before JWT/JTI or API-key fencing. Due batches hold the same guard, lock due Users in UUID order with SKIP LOCKED, and recheck another actually active super-admin before each completion.

NativeInvitationConfig.description: Deployment fallbacks supplied to the owner settings capability.
NativeInvitationConfig.title: NativeInvitationConfig

0242_identity_invitations.schema.json.x-receipts: Success receipts bind operation ID, actor ID (nullable only for public registration), operation, HMAC request fingerprint and derivation epoch. They store token-free result data, no raw bearer/proof/link/password/ciphertext, and have no User or Invitation foreign key.
0242_identity_invitations.schema.json.x-lock-order: Lock participating User authority rows in UUID order using KEY SHARE first; quota creates upgrade the inviter to UPDATE before email. Then acquire the existing email advisory key hashtextextended(email,0), Project, and Invitation/ProjectMember. Project ownership is captured through Workspace before User locks and revalidated while Project remains locked. Batch preview performs the real ordered writes and Audit inside a private PL/pgSQL subtransaction, then rolls it all back with one exact sentinel.
0242_identity_invitations.schema.json.x-outbox: Invitation mail reuses public.identity_credential_mail_outbox with purpose=invitation; outbox.id is the stable send operation ID, actor_id stores issuer, invitation_context stores project snapshot, sender actor triple and typed Audit context. The authoritative raw token stays only on user_invitations; outbox stores the encrypted token, hash and key epoch.

0251_identity_account_locks.schema.json.$comment: Malformed arguments raise SQLSTATE 22023 (invalid_request). Row-lock SQLSTATEs 55P03, 40001, and 40P01 propagate and abort the caller transaction.

AcceptedApiKeyRequest.title: AcceptedApiKeyRequest

0285_identity_accepted_api_key.schema.js.$comment: Confirms an already accepted key ID, not credential possession. The caller retains account/project authority locks. The key FOR SHARE lock waits and remains in the caller transaction. Expiry is checked against the real clock after any lock wait. Invalid arguments raise SQLSTATE 22023; database errors propagate.

0286_identity_read_relations.schema.json.$comment: Fixed read-only owner relations, not authorization decisions. Trusted consumers retain their existing scope predicates, joins, ordering and transaction snapshot. No credential, generation or lifecycle fields are published.

0287_identity_registration_status.schema.$comment: The Recovery owner supplies deployment defaults. read_status resolves the existing Settings policy in a bounded read transaction; read_deployment_default does not read overrides. Neither operation creates accounts, mail, audit events or receipts.

functions.transaction_semantics: Insert one seed persona with the supplied account UUID. This is an insert-only capability and does not authorize the caller, create a Group, write Audit, commit, retry, or upsert. The trusted caller owns persona lookup and the surrounding workflow transaction. Native uniqueness, foreign-key, and length errors propagate.

x-native-capabilities.authorization_boundary: Trusted seed callers retain the production guard and persona lookup; this fixed function adds no application authorization.
x-native-capabilities.transaction_boundary: The caller owns the surrounding transaction and commit.

ScaleSeedActorReply.title: ScaleSeedActorReply

functions.name: read_scale_seed_super_admin
functions.transaction_semantics: Select the earliest-created public.users row with role super_admin. Do not filter is_active or add a tie-breaker; equal created_at values remain unspecified. This read-only STABLE function does not authorize the caller or commit its transaction.

functions.name: read_scale_seed_annotator
functions.transaction_semantics: Select the earliest-created active public.users row whose ID is in the caller-supplied annotator candidate UUID array. Do not apply a platform role filter or add a tie-breaker; equal created_at values remain unspecified. The function does not read Workspace membership or project tables. The caller selects project_member_facts candidates and invokes this STABLE function in the same SQL statement, preserving one statement snapshot across candidate and account reads. This function does not authorize the caller or commit its transaction.

x-native-capabilities.authorization_boundary: Trusted scale-seed callers retain actor selection policy and the surrounding workflow; these fixed read functions add no authorization.
x-native-capabilities.transaction_boundary: The caller owns the transaction. For annotator selection, the candidate UUID array must be selected from Workspace facts inside the same SQL statement that invokes the Identity function.

functions.name: replace_fixture_preferences
functions.transaction_semantics: Replace public.users.preferences for the exact supplied ID, without merge, actor or account-state policy, journaling, retry, or an independent transaction. A matching row counts as one even when the JSON value is unchanged; a NULL or missing ID counts as zero. The UPDATE uses normal row-lock waiting. The caller owns the transaction and commit or rollback.

x-native-capabilities.authorization_boundary: This fixture-only capability is limited by the actual database name ending in _test or _e2e. It performs no actor authentication or account-role, activity, or email check.
x-native-capabilities.transaction_boundary: The caller owns the active transaction, commit, and rollback.

0305_identity_e2e_fixtures.schema.json.$comment: Fixed capabilities for existing guarded E2E fixture routes. These functions accept no arbitrary SQL, table, or predicate selectors.

functions.name: create_account
functions.transaction_semantics: Insert one User with the exact fixture factory defaults: credential_generation 0, active true, offline status, empty preferences, and NULL for other nullable fields. Role and supplied values are not normalized or subject to account policy. Duplicate and native constraint errors propagate. created_at uses the database default. The caller owns the transaction.

functions.name: mark_manual_inactive
functions.transaction_semantics: Set only is_active=false, status=offline, disabled_kind=manual, disabled_at, and disabled_by for the exact ID. A matching row counts as one even when values are unchanged; a missing ID counts as zero. The UPDATE waits for the normal row lock. No actor policy or other User fields are changed. The caller owns the transaction.

functions.name: create_invitations
functions.transaction_semantics: Insert the supplied closed Invitation records without normalizing roles or checking account/project authority. created_at uses the database default. Invitation field, foreign-key, uniqueness, and cast errors propagate. The caller owns the transaction.

functions.name: delete_accounts
functions.transaction_semantics: When shared is true, delete Users matching the fixed email LIKE '%@e2e.test' predicate. Otherwise delete only the exact supplied email array. This function adds no generic predicate or dependent-row cleanup. Native FK errors propagate; the caller owns deletion ordering and the transaction.

functions.name: delete_reset_tokens
functions.transaction_semantics: Delete only PasswordResetToken rows whose user_id is in the exact supplied UUID array. Return the matched row count; the caller owns the transaction.

functions.name: delete_invitations
functions.transaction_semantics: Delete only UserInvitation rows whose invited_by is in the exact supplied UUID array. Return the matched row count; the caller owns the transaction.

functions.name: delete_organization_members
functions.transaction_semantics: Delete only organization_members rows whose user_id is in the exact supplied UUID array. Return the matched row count; the caller owns the transaction and cleanup order.

x-native-capabilities.authorization_boundary: These fixed fixture capabilities check only that the actual database name ends in _test or _e2e. They add no actor, account, project, role, activity, or email authorization policy.
x-native-capabilities.transaction_boundary: The caller owns the active transaction, commit, rollback, and fixture cleanup ordering. These functions never commit or retry.

0454_identity_first_seed_account.schema..title: Identity first seed account attribution
0454_identity_first_seed_account.schema..semantics: Returns zero or one account visible in the current account profile, without filtering role or active state. Selection among multiple accounts is unspecified. The caller owns the transaction.
